solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irritated about catcall, fellow's uncertain regarding place

indicators.note: one word going about others wraps itself around them

parts.note: sore means annoyed or irritated
a mew is the call of a cat
a fellow is referred to as he

explanation.surface: An annoyed person, hearing a catcall, isn't sure where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The irritation word wraps around both the cat's call and the fellow together.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere means in some unspecified location, so it describes being vague about place.

clue.text: Son makes a mark in careers

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to print is to make a mark or impression

explanation.surface: A son making his mark in his chosen professions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like a plural noun about jobs; it is the verb, meaning rushes along.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong, as one sprints, running at full speed.

clue.text: The lead up to fast runs in sporting diagrams

indicators.note: in places the runs letter inside the rearranged letters
sporting suggests playful frolicking, so the letters of diagrams are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A coach studies sports diagrams showing the build-up to a fast break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is not speed but the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, the carnival day, falls just before Lent, the Christian period of fasting.

clue.text: When originally I left company it indicated acquiescence

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of when
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Someone quitting a firm and nodding in agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilco is radio jargon for 'will comply'.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure, wilco signals that a message is understood and will be obeyed, a form of agreement.

clue.text: Disaster area on grand scale — go in but there's a final twist

parts.note: epic means on a grand, heroic scale

indicators.note: a twist at the end means only the last pair of letters is turned round

parts.note: to enter is to go in

explanation.surface: A sweeping drama in which characters walk into a disaster zone, with a twist at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point directly above an earthquake's origin, where the damage is centred.

clue.text: Jeff Lynne's band touring Belgium with another one

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the band name goes round a letter

parts.note: Jeff Lynne led the Electric Light Orchestra
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
W is an abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Jeff Lynne's band on tour in Belgium alongside another group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' refers back to band: Elbow is a Manchester rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow is a British rock group, so it is another band besides ELO.

clue.text: 28 garret

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the answer to 28 across, Greek, here as an adjective; of Athens, the ancient Greek dialect or style
second meaning: a room in the roof space at the top of a house

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads '28 garret' as a Greek garret, but 28 stands alone as one meaning: Attic is Athenian, hence Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes ancient Athens and its dialect, so it is Greek in that sense, and an attic is also a loft room.

clue.text: It's substantial taking recurrent strain of a risky business

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding the other piece inside

parts.note: actual means real, having substance

indicators.note: recurrent suggests running back, so the strain is read the other way

parts.note: a strain of music is an air, a tune

explanation.surface: A recurring strain is part and parcel of a hazardous trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuarial work calculates insurance risk, so the word describes the business of assessing hazards.

clue.text: Tether ram that is brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a tup is a ram
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ram is tethered and brought into the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up an animal is to tether it, fastening it with a rope.

clue.text: Caught old Robin dancing vivaciously

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of Robin are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old man named Robin is caught dancing with great energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is an Italian musical direction meaning with spirit and vigour.

clue.text: Country right by Russian river

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
the Ural flows from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: A countryside scene next to a river in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country life, means rural.

clue.text: In pub small wager at first is within limits

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed in the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the wager is to be placed first, ahead of the word for small

parts.note: a bet is a wager
wee means small

explanation.surface: Placing a small bet in a pub is kept within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' puts the wager ahead of 'small', even though the clue reads them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: In-between describes something lying inside two bounds, intermediate.

clue.text: Unpleasant feeling returns for second time? On the contrary

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so read backwards

indicators.text: for second time? On the contrary
indicators.note: taken literally the phrase swaps one letter for another, and the contrary flips which replaces which

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling
T is the abbreviation for time
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An unpleasant emotion comes back a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T for S' would put T in place of S; on the contrary, S replaces the T of EMOTION, giving EMOSION, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome is a synonym of offensive or disgusting, especially of smells.

clue.text: With 50 Cent say Hershey Bar comes included in this

definitions.text: Hershey Bar comes included in this

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for with
50 Cent is an American rapper, 'say' marking an example

explanation.surface: The rapper 50 Cent endorsing a Hershey chocolate bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Hershey is a US chocolate maker; the definition is a description of what a confectionery bar comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate bar is sold inside a paper or foil covering, so the bar is included in it.

clue.text: Character's decorative foot brings passions back

indicators.note: brought back means turned round to read the other way

parts.note: fires are passions, ardent feelings

explanation.surface: Someone's ornamental foot rekindles old passions.
explanation.walkthrough: The character is a printed letter, not a person, and its foot is the stroke at the base.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small finishing stroke on a letter's strokes in typography.

clue.text: Raw material for manufacture of iron and dockets with slips

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: slips means slides out of place, so the letters of dockets are disordered

explanation.surface: A factory's supplies of iron, plus delivery dockets and paper slips.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedstock is the unprocessed material supplied to an industrial process.

clue.text: Becoming fond of nursing student in lecture

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles the other

parts.note: to take to someone is to come to like them
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A teacher growing fond of a student while giving a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a reprimand, which is the sense of lecture as a telling-off.

clue.text: Glower as gentle sob rises up?

parts.note: light means gentle, as in a light touch

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to blub is to sob

explanation.surface: Someone glowers as a soft sob rises up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' reads as a scowl, but it is split as glow-er, a thing that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bulb glows, so it is literally a glower in this whimsical sense.

clue.text: Seeing head of government tired with cough

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of government
limp means drooping, tired
to cough and to sing are both slang for confessing to police

explanation.surface: A worn-out head of government with a cough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cough' looks like illness but is slang for confess, as is sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Glimpsing means catching sight of something briefly, a kind of seeing.

clue.text: Seasonal treat, like gathering Michaelmas daisy for instance

indicators.note: gathering means taking in and holding something

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so like
the Michaelmas daisy is a kind of aster
e.g. is short for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A seasonal treat, perhaps picking autumn daisies.
explanation.walkthrough: The first EG wraps around both the flower and the second EG. A Michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster, Michaelmas being 29 September.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg is a traditional confection given at Easter time.

clue.text: Magician's bird flies up but with court card for head — that's conjuring

indicators.note: for head means the bird's head letter is swapped out for the card
in a down clue, flying up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a dove is the bird a stage magician produces from a hat or sleeve
a king is a court card in a pack

explanation.surface: A conjuror's bird flutters upward, and a king card appears in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of the bird is D, which ends up last once DOVE is turned to EVOD; KING replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a spirit is to conjure it up, call it forth by magic.

clue.text: Scottish port is part of isle, I think

indicators.note: the answer is said to be a part of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of isle, all of I, and the start of think

explanation.surface: Someone guessing that a Scottish harbour lies on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is Edinburgh's port on the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: This man initially experiments with fruit — sounds like an ass …

parts.note: this man is he

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the first letter of experiments
haws are hawthorn berries

explanation.surface: A man experimenting with fruit makes a fool of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' is not a homophone here: it is the definition, the noise a donkey makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haws are the braying noises of a donkey, which is an ass.

clue.text: Becoming absorbed by large flowerless plant seen around island

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a large clothing size

indicators.note: the plant is placed around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: moss reproduces by spores and has no flowers
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Getting absorbed by a large moss growing on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the passage of a solvent through a membrane, and figuratively the gradual absorption of ideas.

clue.text: … — tree's first of modified fruit with no core

indicators.note: taking out the core removes the middle letter
first of points to the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of modified
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a tree bearing altered fruit that has been cored.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to 20 down's fruit. Coring APPLE takes out its middle P.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a deciduous tree known for its leaves and sap.

clue.text: One short month with Southern clans

parts.note: Sept is the shortened form of September
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Southern clans gathering for one brief month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short month' suggests February, but it means a month's abbreviated name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a branch of an Irish or Scottish clan, a family division.

clue.text: Public transport? Please, that's not half a squash

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea on a crowded tram: please, it's a terrible crush.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of PLEASE survives. 'Squash' suggests a crowd on the tram, but it is a verb meaning crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread down and crush, which is to squash.

clue.text: Haloes are beaten gold on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top places the gold symbol above the rest

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: beaten means hammered out of shape, so the letters of are are rearranged

explanation.surface: Saints' haloes are made of beaten gold leaf laid on the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurae is a plural of aura, a glowing light surrounding a figure.

clue.text: I mark concert, put out by unrehearsed piece

parts.note: M is short for the German mark, a currency
a prom is a promenade concert

indicators.note: out means in disarray, so the letters of put are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic marking a concert is put off by an improvised number.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu is a musical piece that sounds spontaneous, as if made up on the spot.

clue.text: An Indian dish from e.g. Madhur Jaffrey broadcast?

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read

parts.note: Madhur Jaffrey is a cookery writer, said in a non-rhotic British accent

explanation.surface: An Indian dish presented on TV by the cookery writer Madhur Jaffrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Madhur Jaffrey is an Indian actress and cookery writer famous for TV programmes; the sound match needs the British accent that drops the final r.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: Bad odour following Grand National?

indicators.note: following means placed after, setting the order of pieces

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a reek is a strong unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: A stench at the Grand National horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase; here Grand and National are split, National being a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek is a citizen of Greece, a national of that country, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Dunks beer mugs washed up with last of slops

indicators.note: washing up tumbles the mugs about in the sink, mixing their order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of slops

explanation.surface: Beer mugs in the sink with the last of the slops.
explanation.definitionFit: To dunk is to dip or plunge something under a liquid, which is to submerge it.
